deep.reconstruction:
Setting. K is a 1-dimensional combinatorial 'system of pseudolines' indexed by a set I. It is a graph together with a family (K_i) of cycles, the pseudolines, pairwise meeting in exactly one vertex. From the previous page, Grothendieck wants to show that when K comes from an actual 2-dimensional arrangement X in the projective plane, the 2-dimensional ('orientation') data can be recovered from (K,(K_i)) alone.

The 3-line case and its ambiguity. Take J in P_3(I), a 3-element subset, giving a 'triangle' subsystem K_J: three pseudolines, pairwise intersecting but not concurrent. Its 1-skeleton has 3 vertices, and each pair of vertices is joined by two edges. A 2-cell structure on RP^2 compatible with it consists of 4 triangles. These are chosen among the 8 possible triangular cycles (one edge from each of the 3 double edges), and they form one of the two 'parity classes'. So the 1-dimensional data of 3 lines does not determine the 2-dimensional arrangement. There are exactly two completions, and choosing one is what he calls the 'orientation' of K_J.

Case 1: a fourth pseudoline Δ = D_i avoids all three vertices of K_J. Then K_{J∪{i}} is a simple arrangement of 4 pseudolines (no three concurrent).

The Proposition. The forgetful functor (simple general arrangements of 4 pseudolines, 2-dimensional) → (simple 1-dimensional arrangements of 4 pseudolines) is an equivalence of categories. His proof sketch: compare both groupoids with the groupoid of 4-element sets.

Check of the Proposition. 1-dimensional side:
- The underlying graph has vertices = the 6 pairs from {1..4}, with each line contributing a 3-cycle. This is the octahedron graph K_{2,2,2} with a distinguished alternating set of 4 triangular faces.
- An automorphism fixing every line fixes every vertex and every edge, so it is trivial.
- The automorphism group is therefore S_4, acting faithfully on the lines.

2-dimensional side:
- 4 generic lines in RP^2 give 6 vertices, 12 edges, 4 triangles and 3 quadrilaterals (Euler characteristic 1). This is the tetrahemihexahedron.
- The cells added are the other 4 octahedral triangles plus 3 quadrilaterals.
- The arrangement is unique up to isomorphism, with combinatorial automorphism group S_4.

Both groupoids are connected with group S_4, and the functor is bijective on automorphisms, so it is an equivalence.

Consequence. Since K_{J∪{i}} canonically comes from a 2-dimensional arrangement, deleting Δ induces a 2-cell structure on K_J. This gives an orientation ε_{J,i}. The next page states (A5): this orientation is independent of the choice of i. Case 2 (every other line passes through a vertex of the triangle) is treated there via a 9-point, 6-line configuration.

What this serves. A local-to-global reconstruction: the cell structure of a pseudoline arrangement is determined by its 1-skeleton together with the line cycles, by gluing canonical orientations of all 3-element subarrangements. In modern terms, the chirotope / oriented-matroid data on triples is recovered from local cyclic-order data.
errors: 'formé de trois ps. droites concourantes' must mean pairwise intersecting (concurrent two by two), not all through one point; otherwise K_J would not be a triangle.

The Proposition depends on how 'simple 1-dimensional arrangement' is defined. It holds if the objects are graphs with 4 distinguished 3-cycles pairwise meeting in one vertex, i.e. the octahedron with 4 alternating faces. Without that structure, the automorphism group of the bare octahedron graph would be 48, not 24.

The proof is only sketched ('en comparant les groupoïdes à celui des ensembles à 4 éléments'). It also needs the uniqueness of the simple arrangement of 4 pseudolines up to isomorphism, which is true but not argued here.
The 'orientation' is not literally an orientation, since RP^2 is non-orientable. It is a choice between the two parity classes of triangles, i.e. a sign/chirality; the terminology may confuse.

ideas.what: Equivalence of categories between simple 2-dimensional arrangements of 4 pseudolines and their 1-dimensional (graph plus line-cycles) skeletons, proved by identifying both groupoids with the groupoid of 4-element sets.
ideas.modern_name: Rigidity / reconstruction of a pseudoline arrangement from its 1-skeleton; uniqueness of the simple 4-line arrangement (tetrahemihexahedron) with automorphism group S_4
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in oriented matroid theory (Björner–Las Vergnas–Sturmfels–White–Ziegler); reconstruction from local sequences is due to Goodman–Pollack and Felsner

ideas.what: Canonical 'orientation' (choice of one of two 2-cell completions) of a triangle of 3 pseudolines, induced by a fourth line in general position, with independence of the choice of fourth line (A5, next page).
ideas.modern_name: Chirotope sign of a triple in a rank-3 oriented matroid / local-to-global recovery of chirotope from local cyclic orders
ideas.usually_credited_to: Oriented matroid theory (Folkman–Lawrence 1978, Bland–Las Vergnas); local sequences: Goodman–Pollack, Felsner–Weil
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to work on pseudoline configurations, but this construction is not published there as far as I know.

ideas.what: Use of groupoids/categories of arrangements, and of functors 2-dim → 1-dim structures, as the framework for combinatorial geometry of arrangements.
ideas.modern_name: Groupoid-theoretic / categorical treatment of combinatorial types of arrangements
ideas.usually_credited_to: Not standard in the oriented-matroid literature

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates the reconstruction of a pseudoline arrangement from its 1-dimensional data as a gluing of rigid 4-line pieces along an equivalence of groupoids. This is a categorical/descent-style version of reconstructing a rank-3 chirotope from local data. The oriented-matroid literature does this purely combinatorially, without the groupoid viewpoint.
missed.quote: est une équivalence de catégories. (On le démontre en comparant les deux groupoïdes, à celui des arr. 4 éléments)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests a stack-like or descent formulation: arrangements as objects glued from the 4-element rigid pieces, with obstructions in the 3-element pieces. This could connect to recent work on moduli of oriented matroids and to the combinatorial anabelian themes of the Esquisse. Value is modest; the underlying facts are known.

missed.claim: Grothendieck flags that the case where some pseudoline is a digon (only one other line crossing it in two points) needs separate treatment and was not verified.
missed.quote: Je n'ai donc pas vérifié que la proposition ci-dessus soit correcte, sans exclure le cas où K est formé de n pseudo-droites concourantes, coupées par une seule autre ps. droite. (previous page)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor edge case. Completing it is routine in oriented-matroid terms.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is correct and elegantly framed: a groupoid equivalence for the rigid 4-line arrangement, and orientations of triangles induced by a fourth line. The underlying mathematics (rigidity of the simple 4-line arrangement, reconstruction of chirotopes from local data) is known in oriented matroid theory. Only the categorical framing is distinctively Grothendieckian.
transcription_corrections: 'arr. 4 éléments' at the end of the parenthesis likely reads 'à celui des ens. à 4 éléments' (groupoid of 4-element sets), with 'fini' crossed out.
The crossed-out insertion above 'catégorie des arr. généraux' appears to read 'foncteurs, ... de ... vers ...' — uncertain.
'soit formé' should read 'soit formé' / 'soient formés' (grammatical agreement); the meaning is a system of 4 pseudolines, no three concurrent.
The orientation symbol at the bottom is probably ω_{J,i} (consistent with the next page's ω_{Ji}) rather than ε_{J,i}.
